intro.title: Cart Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a shopping cart feature for an Angular e-commerce app using a service to manage shared state. You'll learn how to create an Angular service that acts as a central context, holding cart items and providing methods to add and remove them. This involves key Angular constructs like services, dependency injection, and RxJS BehaviorSubject for reactive state. By the end, you'll have a functional cart that multiple components can access and update consistently.
intro.usecase: Cart context is essential for e-commerce platforms like Amazon or Shopify, where users add items to a cart while browsing. This pattern manages cart state—such as items, quantities, and totals—across multiple components like product listings, cart summaries, and checkout pages. Developers use cart context to avoid prop drilling and ensure consistent cart data updates, enhancing user experience in shopping flows. It's also applied in booking systems for hotels or flights, where selections must persist across different UI sections.
